note: Date = when the study was run or first saved on the research branch. The period each study tested is shown on its card.

entries.title: Live review: recommendations and paper trades, 5-14 Oct 2026
entries.asked: How did the journal's recommendations and the paper trades do on the first eight live days?
entries.result: 32 logged recommendations were only 5 distinct ideas (4 positive on the index, 1 stopped). 15 paper trades netted about +₹22.6k, but one trade made 117% of it.
entries.summary: Repeated re-logging inflates the counts (20 of the 32 rows were the same Nifty put idea on 8 Oct). A positive index result did not always mean an option profit (a Bank Nifty idea at +0.37R lost 8.8% on the premium). All five 45-minute time-stop exits lost; the winners held to 15:15. Several signal trades (for example on 7 and 12 Oct) have no matching journal recommendation. Eight days is too few to change any rule.

entries.title: Lower-circuit stocks
entries.asked: Should stocks locked on their lower circuit be recommended?
entries.result: 8% of rule signals closed on a lower-circuit signature; 22% of those were locked again from the next open, so they could not be sold.
entries.summary: On 15 Oct two picks (STLTECH, HFCL) closed on the 5% lower circuit. The backtest assumes you can always sell, so it flatters them. The nightly scan now skips such stocks and lists them as skipped; the 9:30 live check also flags a stock on its lower circuit. Without them the backtest unseen return fell from 11.3% to 7.7% a year, which is the honest price of not holding unsellable stock.

entries.title: Round 17: 'put 60% of the account into every recommended option'
entries.asked: What would bigger position sizes do to the account?
entries.result: At 60% the typical worst fall is -94%; today's 1% risk gave x1.82 with -17% worst fall.
entries.summary: The same 922 trades were re-sized as a real account. Every step up in size bought more upside with a bigger fall; 2% risk compounding was the most that still looked like an account. A premium cut-off adds nothing because the spot stop already acts as one.

entries.title: Does a gap at the next open change the rule?
entries.asked: Should the live check warn on gap-ups or gap-downs?
entries.result: No: gap-up over 3% still hit 61%; gap-down 1-3% hit 83% (+3.4% average).
entries.summary: 2,011 historical rule signals, bought at the actual next open. A gap in either direction did not hurt, so the 9:30 live check shows the gap but only flags a price already below the stop or already at the target.

entries.title: Our stock rule vs platform-style signals vs the Nifty
entries.asked: Is our BUY rule stronger than the candle, momentum and breakout signals platforms show?
entries.result: Rule pick 23.5% a year (training) and 11.7% (unseen) with falls of -14% and -4%; candle rules 5% at best and negative unseen; Nifty 8.7% / -9.3%.
entries.summary: Momentum shows 31-91% a year but on today's index list in a strong trend year, with deeper falls (-28% to -37%), so it is survivorship-inflated. The BUY rule is the only one to beat the Nifty in both periods with a small fall.

entries.title: Candle patterns on 10 big stocks and the 100 most liquid
entries.asked: Do pin bars, engulfing and inside-bar signals work on large Indian stocks?
entries.result: No edge: excess return near zero (t between -1.4 and +1.0), inside-bar breakout long worse than a random day (t -2.7).
entries.summary: Fixed 1/3/5/10-day holds and a book-style 2:1 stop-and-target both tried, with trend and 20-day-extreme context. Bracket win rates were 36-40% vs 33-35% for random days, with average reward near zero. This is the test of the Candlestick Trading Bible's core idea.

entries.title: Review of 'The Candlestick Trading Bible' (PDF)
entries.asked: How useful is the book for the algo?
entries.result: Low as a trading system, medium as beginner education.
entries.summary: No backtests; examples are hand-picked forex charts; most of it is discretionary (support/resistance, Fibonacci, supply/demand). Its useful parts (higher-timeframe context, 2:1 minimum reward-to-risk, 1-2% risk, avoiding chop) are already in the rules. Its core claim was tested on 100 stocks and failed.

entries.title: Round 16: cash-equity rules on the Nifty 500
entries.asked: Which stock rules (momentum, 52-week high, pullbacks, mean reversion) beat the Nifty?
entries.result: Only one beat the Nifty on both halves: buy a 10% three-day drop above the 200-day average, +5% target, out after 5 days. 64% hit, 24% a year in training, 11.5% unseen, worst fall 4-14%.
entries.summary: This is the stock rule behind the BUY picks. Momentum and breakout rules looked far bigger but were survivorship bias (today's index list). Plan on 8-12% a year, not the backtest's 20-24%. The rule is uncorrelated with the option rules (-0.08 to -0.16).

entries.title: Round 15: an LLM multi-agent trading desk
entries.asked: Can an AI 'trading desk' (analysts, bull vs bear, risk team) beat the rules?
entries.result: 58 trades, -₹1.0k, PF 0.99 against +₹19.3k for the rules on the same 60 sessions.
entries.summary: It matched the rules' direction 34 of 35 times but lost the difference on exits. As a filter ('desk agrees') it showed +₹28.3k on 37 trades, one half-year only, so it is a watch-list lead.

entries.title: Round 14D: verification of the expiry-day straddle
entries.asked: Does 14B's number survive an independent rebuild?
entries.result: Reproduced (+₹193k with real lot sizes), but the top 10 days are 65% of the net and the tail is about 15x the average day.
entries.summary: The decay gap between expiry and non-expiry days is real. The edge is a roughly 22-point premium a day for carrying a -300 to -340 point tail. Worth an off-by-default paper strategy with a gap/event filter, not a live one.

entries.title: Round 14C: market-structure inputs
entries.asked: Do cross-index, breadth, relative strength, flow proxy or implied-move inputs improve the rules?
entries.result: 0 of 32 filters, inverses and votes beat the baseline on both halves.
entries.summary: Agreement between inputs was real but tiny (+2 to +3 basis points to the close) and the rules already require VWAP agreement, so each filter removed more good trades than bad. Watch-list: trading the laggard index, and breakouts after the implied move is spent.

entries.title: Round 14B: expiry-day option selling on real prices
entries.asked: Does selling straddles on expiry days make money?
entries.result: Nifty expiry-day straddle +₹218k over 157 days (PF 1.67) after a 2.7% entry haircut, with days of -₹15k to -₹22k.
entries.summary: A real edge from fast decay on expiry days, but concentrated in quiet days: the 21 days with a move over 1% gave back ₹232k. Shipping would need sell-side orders, margin checks and an event filter. Not shippable on this evidence alone.

entries.title: Round 14A: re-entry after a stop, pyramiding, extra trend-day trades
entries.asked: Do re-entries or adding to winners help?
entries.result: Pyramiding looked bigger (₹241.8k) but only because of 1.6x exposure and a 57% drawdown; trend-day extras almost never trigger.
entries.summary: Re-entering after a stop was flat-to-negative except opposite-direction Camarilla (15 training trades, none unseen). 'Trend day confirmed' is only known too late to trade on. The app stays at one trade per rule per day.

entries.title: Quick check: ORB + VWAP + volume, Crabel NR7, Raschke Holy Grail
entries.asked: Do three suggested strategies work?
entries.result: All three failed: ORB lost ₹68k (Nifty) and ₹233k (Bank Nifty); NR7 days were worse for breakouts, not better.
entries.summary: The ORB with VWAP filters was the app's original rulebook. Holy Grail fired only 12-21 times in 3¾ years and lost on Nifty at every setting.

entries.title: Candlestick check: 12 textbook patterns on daily stocks
entries.asked: Do hammer, engulfing, stars, doji and harami predict moves?
entries.result: None of the 12 beat random days with the same context on both halves.
entries.summary: After a 5-day fall every day averaged +1.89% over 10 days; it is the drop, not the candle shape. As a filter on the 10%-drop rule candles only subtracted.

entries.title: Round 13: sizing, exits, strike, re-entry, Bank Nifty settings, Market Profile
entries.asked: Can sizing, exits, strikes, re-entries, Bank Nifty tuning or Market Profile improve the book?
entries.result: Nothing beat the current rules on both the training and unseen halves; Market Profile entries lost every year.
entries.summary: Lead worth re-testing: sizing up when VIX is in its 50-75th percentile (the only scheme better on both halves, but ₹59.7k of the ₹60.6k unseen profit came from that one band). Exits, 1-ITM strike and Nifty-tuned settings on Bank Nifty all stay.

entries.title: Round 12: nine recorded live sessions
entries.asked: What do the first recorded live days show about real prices and open interest?
entries.result: The formula under-prices 1-day-to-expiry options by about 15%; bid-ask spread is only 0.26% of premium; OI and volume leads need 40+ sessions.
entries.summary: Nine sessions (28 Sep to 9 Oct) is a sample for leads, not proof. The journal then showed 13 distinct recommendations (the same idea had been logged repeatedly before a fix). The AI was retrained to 2026-10-01; neural nets, forests and other model families all landed between profit factor 0.7 and 1.1.

entries.title: Round 9: EMA + volume + RSI combinations
entries.asked: Do moving-average and RSI combos with volume find a robust edge?
entries.result: 3 robust settings on training, 0 profitable on the unseen 120 days.
entries.summary: 1,200 of 5,250 settings were tried (5 average types, entry styles, RSI rules, relative volume, exits). The volume filter looked helpful only because it removed trades, not because it picked better ones.

entries.title: Round 11: rules from a web review, on 1-minute data
entries.asked: Do last-half-hour momentum, initial-balance, time-of-day and VIX-gate ideas work?
entries.result: Last-half-hour momentum and the initial-balance trade lost; the VIX floor stays at 11.
entries.summary: Last-half-hour momentum won 50-52% but under 1 index point a trade, so decay and costs ate it. The initial-balance extension trade lost in every variant. A VIX 'above 14 only' gate looked good in training but lost on the unseen half, so it was not adopted.

entries.title: Round 10: VWAP + EMA + RSI + ADX + volume + ATR + CPR + OI in every combination
entries.asked: Does any combination of 8 indicators add to the rules?
entries.result: 24 robust combos, 8 positive on unseen days but on only 6-8 trades each.
entries.summary: 2,572 runs. The best survivors (VWAP cross with ATR expansion, volume and put/call ratio) had unseen samples too small to conclude. 4-5 confirmations were best; 'k of 8' votes lost at every k. Re-test after about 60 more sessions.

entries.title: Round 8: an AI model instead of rules
entries.asked: Can a machine-learning model beat the rules?
entries.result: 3-seed average +₹21k over 2024-26 (2025 negative) against +₹192k for the rules.
entries.summary: LightGBM was trained on 111,630 decision points with 64 inputs and judged walk-forward. Variants that predicted the move to the close or learned entries with the rules' exits showed no skill. It ships only as an optional, off-by-default 'AI model'. In-sample the same model shows 90%+ wins, which is a trap.

entries.title: Round 7: 80-120 point rallies, scalping and stop behaviour
entries.asked: Is there something in intraday rallies, scalping or smarter stops?
entries.result: 0 of 1,458 scalping rules made money; wider, tighter or profit-booking stops all earned less than the current stop.
entries.summary: Nifty makes about three 80+ point moves a day, but nothing reliably predicts where they start. Of trades that touched the stop, 49% came back to entry, but widening the stop earned less. No sign of stop hunting beyond chance.

entries.title: Round 6: stress tests of the two strategies
entries.asked: How fragile are the two rules?
entries.result: Rolled Nifty to the next expiry at 1 day left; no new signals on Budget day; 1% risk kept. A normal year: median +₹55.7k, 13.5% of years negative.
entries.summary: Tests covered expiry effects, late entry (a 1-minute delay made no measurable difference), a luck test with 5,000 one-year paths, event days, trend vs range days and real contract history. All profit came from trend days (36% of days); range days lost. VIX above 20 at the open lost.

entries.title: Round 5: more families, and stacking filters
entries.asked: Do more strategy types, or stacking confirmation filters, add accuracy?
entries.result: Camarilla H4/L4 breakout passed and now runs alongside the noise rule (every year positive); stacking filters only overfit (win rate 35.4% to 35.8%).
entries.summary: EMA stacks, MACD, Bollinger, candle reversals, Heikin-Ashi, Donchian and VWAP bands were tested. Only the Camarilla breakout held up. 395 filter combinations were tried on the noise rule: 134 beat it on training, only 3 on unseen days. Running two different strategies together (daily correlation about 0.3) helped; piling filters onto one did not.

entries.title: Round 4: check option prices against real NSE prices
entries.asked: Is the formula-priced option profit realistic?
entries.result: The formula priced 3-14 day options about 9.5% too high; real options decayed faster on sideways days. After correcting, buying 1 strike in-the-money beat at-the-money.
entries.summary: Profit was recomputed against 52,191 real NSE closing option prices over 735 days and 5,592 real 5-minute holding windows. Implied volatility and an extra per-hour decay charge were corrected. The same strategy still won, and the rule changed to buy 1 strike ITM. On 11 recent trades real P&L was ₹3.7k vs ₹7.3k from the formula, a reminder that the backtest is on the optimistic side.

entries.title: Small accounts (₹15,000, one lot per signal)
entries.asked: Can a ₹15,000 account follow the rules?
entries.result: Nifty 1-OTM made money every year but fell up to 47% from a peak; the worst single trade lost ₹5.7k.
entries.summary: The 1% rule allows ₹150 of risk, but one lot risks ₹1,500-6,000, so the normal backtest takes no trades. With always-one-lot, results were positive but the account could be cut roughly in half on a bad run. Bank Nifty lots mostly cost more than ₹15,000.

entries.title: Round 3: strategies popular Indian F&O creators teach
entries.asked: Do the strategies taught online (5 EMA, 44 MA, inside-bar, Fibonacci, RSI 60/40, multi-timeframe breakout) beat the chosen rule?
entries.result: Every one lost on the unseen 120 days (-₹3k to -₹112k) against +₹19.6k for the chosen rule.
entries.summary: Six popular creator strategies were coded as taught and run through the same 400-setting loop. Walk-forward Fibonacci (+₹26k) and 5 EMA (+₹13k) were about break-even per trade; the rest were negative. Option selling and OI-driven methods could not be tested with free data.

entries.title: Rounds 1-2: find the best intraday strategy
entries.asked: Which of 9 popular intraday strategies makes money on days it was never tuned on?
entries.result: Noise-area momentum won: +₹19.6k on the last 120 unseen days (both indices) while the old opening-range rules lost ₹125k.
entries.summary: Nine strategy families (opening-range breakouts, VWAP pullbacks, Supertrend, previous-day levels, EMA/ADX, gap trades, iron fly and noise-area momentum) were run in about 5,000 settings on 3¾ years of 5-minute data, with all costs. Settings were chosen on 2023 to April 2026 and judged on the last 120 sessions they never saw. Nifty was profitable every year; Bank Nifty lost in 2025; most single stocks lost, so the indices are preferred.

entries.title: Market recorder started
entries.asked: What can't be backtested from free history?
entries.result: Recording began on 28 Sep 2026: option chains every 5 minutes, 1-minute data and participant positioning every evening.
entries.summary: Expired-option prices, bid/ask spreads, chain open interest and FII/DII positioning are not available for past dates, so the app and a nightly GitHub job now save them as they happen for later studies.
